title: Probability
notes: This chapter covers THEORETICAL (classical) probability only -- based on equally likely outcomes, not experimental/observed frequency.
P(E) = (Number of outcomes favourable to E) / (Total number of possible outcomes) -- the single formula this entire chapter is built on.
P(E) + P(not E) = 1, so P(not E) = 1 - P(E). 'Not E' is called the complement of E.
Probability of an impossible event = 0. Probability of a sure/certain event = 1.
0 <= P(E) <= 1 always -- a probability can NEVER be negative or greater than 1. Great way to instantly spot wrong answers.

Common experiment setups to know cold: single die (6 outcomes), pair of dice (36 outcomes), deck of 52 cards (4 suits x 13 ranks, 12 face cards, 26 red/26 black), coin toss (2 outcomes, HH/HT/TH/TT for two coins).
'Without replacement' problems (cards/pens/bulbs removed and not put back) change the total number of outcomes for the next draw -- always recompute the denominator.

examples.question: A bag contains only lemon-flavoured candies. What's the probability of drawing an orange-flavoured one?
examples.solution: 0 -- it's an impossible event since the bag has no orange candies at all.

exercises.question: Which of these cannot be the probability of an event? (A) 2/3 (B) -1.5 (C) 15% (D) 0.7
If P(E) = 0.05, what is P(not E)?
Probability of 2 students NOT sharing a birthday (in a group of 3) is 0.992. Find probability they DO share a birthday.
A bag has 3 red and 5 black balls. Find probability of drawing (i) red (ii) not red.
A die is thrown once. Find probability of getting: (i) a prime number (ii) a number between 2 and 6 (iii) an odd number.
One card drawn from a 52-card deck. Find probability of: (i) a red king (ii) a face card (iii) a red face card (iv) jack of hearts (v) a spade (vi) queen of diamonds.
12 defective pens mixed with 132 good ones. One pen drawn at random. Find probability it's good.
A box has discs numbered 1-90. Find probability the drawn disc has: (i) a two-digit number (ii) a perfect square number (iii) a number divisible by 5.
A die's six faces show letters A,B,C,D,E,A. Find probability of getting: (i) A (ii) D.
